sources.claim: An authenticated caller needs invocation permission on the receiving Cloud Run service; service-to-service identity and target permission must be checked together.
The configured Cloud Run service identity is used by running code for Google API access and is distinct from deployment identity unless explicitly configured the same.
storage.objects.get permits reading object data and metadata; Cloud Run invocation permission does not provide that dependency permission.

a.conclusion: The authenticated caller lacks run.routes.invoke on the exact receiving service and is rejected before container dispatch. Runtime dependency access is separately supported by the policy review and successful refresh, so a runtime storage grant does not explain these two failures.
next_checks: Name the caller and receiving service as the failed permission boundary, preserving the distinction from runtime, deployer and service agent.
Sam confirms the intended caller/service binding and relevant change history, then proposes only the needed service-scoped invocation access to the authorized change owner.
Avery verifies a subsequent owner-authorized request reaches the handler and completes, without obtaining or printing tokens.
unsupported: The runtime service account lacks storage.objects.get and caused these pre-handler responses.
Granting storage access to the caller or invoker access to the runtime fixes the recorded boundary.
Grant project Owner/Editor, make the service public, or print a token.
The application or user impact has recovered.
unknowns: Why the caller's expected invocation permission is absent and whether it is intended.
Recovery after the two denied requests.

b.conclusion: Invocation succeeds and both requests enter the handler. The configured runtime service account is denied storage.objects.get on the existing dependency object, and the application maps that failure to the caller's HTTP 403. This is a dependency authorization boundary, not caller invocation failure.
next_checks: Correlate handler-entry, runtime principal, dependency resource/permission and mapped response for both IDs.
Sam and Taylor confirm the intended runtime identity and least-privilege read access on the required bucket/object boundary; return a scoped proposal to the change owner.
Avery asks for a subsequent authorized request's handler, dependency and completion metadata before claiming recovery.
unsupported: The caller lacks roles/run.invoker or the request failed before the handler.
Changing the deployer or service-agent role repairs runtime object access.
Grant project Owner/Editor, expose tokens, fetch rule contents, or make the service public.
An allowed invocation proves successful business execution or recovery.
unknowns: Why the runtime principal lacks dependency access or whether it is the intended principal.
